title: Choose Eve's visual world
question: Five takes on the same screen: the organizer inbox for Cal Hacks 13.0, with sample data. Pick the one Eve's design system should grow from, or re-roll.

options.label: Blue Hour
options.lineage: Eve as evening: civil twilight over an overnight hackathon
options.thesis: Event money gets decided after dark, so urgency reads as colour temperature, from cool blue to dusk apricot.
options.viewport: Indigo rail and dusk ground; the inbox ranks items by deadline, and each row's left edge and due chip take that deadline's temperature.
options.risk: If the indigo slides toward black or the warm end turns neon, this becomes the generic dark AI dashboard.

raised.raise: Density: claims and people render all 300 attendees in compact whole rows; nothing is paged away.
Capacity: every cap and budget line shows its running total pressed against its limit.
Fixed scale: gross, withholding, fees, and net drawn as one bar on one scale, so net is visibly what is left.
Figures: every amount in full-contrast tabular numerals, right-aligned to the decimal.

options.label: Tick & Tie
options.lineage: auditors' working papers: tick marks that tie each figure to its source
options.thesis: Every amount carries an auditor's tick you can follow to its evidence: green for receipt, blue for bank, red for exception.
materials: Public Sans, the US government's typeface
options.viewport: Graphite side rail, white work area; inbox rows carry amounts with tick marks, and a tick legend sits in the footer.
options.risk: It is the closest to the clean-fintech default; the ticks are the main thing separating it from Ramp or Mercury.

options.label: Course & Controls
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps: fixed terrain colours, purple course on top
options.thesis: Policy is fixed terrain; each payout runs a purple course of numbered controls (form, withholding, approval, release), punched off as they clear.
materials: purple reserved for the active path
options.viewport: White ground, purple-keyed top bar; each inbox item shows its payout course as numbered circles joined by purple legs, with the stalled control ringed.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: a payout becomes a course of controls, and 'the course never edits the terrain' matches 'the agent never changes policy.' It holds clarity but loses audience identification, since orienteering is not hackathon culture.
options.risk: If course circles spread past the payout path, it turns into a map gimmick.

options.label: Action Colour
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, with one saturated colour that appears only on what you can press, so a blocked approval visibly loses it.
materials: action colour reserved for live controls
options.viewport: Warm ground and a light top bar; the inbox is a single column of roomy cards, and only live buttons carry the orange.
options.case: Its rule matches the PRD's 'disabled with a reason' approvals, so it holds clarity. It loses audience identification with controllers who work dense queues.
options.risk: Roomy cards waste density on a 300-person claim queue, and cream plus orange is a look many AI-built apps share.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Every attendee as a stamp-sized cell in one numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid of attendees keyed to table codes.
options.case: Organizers and controllers don't identify with convention catalogs, and the grid hides money states.
options.risk: Newsprint texture reads as costume on a finance screen.
options.kept: Density: all 300 attendees visible in compact whole rows.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Budgets as tape sides that must not overflow.
options.viewport: Side A and side B lists, with running totals tight to the margin.
options.case: Handwriting and ruled stock undermine trust in figures, and no role identifies with it.
options.risk: Ruled paper standing in for a table is a costume.
options.kept: Capacity: running totals pressed against each cap.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A claim's life stages drawn as same-scale plates.
options.viewport: Five aligned plates from submitted to paid.
options.case: Cream and engraved serifs land in a known AI cluster, and the plates slow down queue work.
options.risk: Reads as a museum, not a money tool.
options.kept: Fixed scale: the payout breakdown on one shared scale.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black-and-white data density in one monospace face.
options.viewport: Columns of numerals over a barcode field.
options.case: No colour means no state colours, and strobing has no place in approvals.
options.risk: Unreadable for attendees and tiring for long sessions.
options.kept: Figures: tabular numerals at full contrast.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What spend-management dashboards ship, done properly: white, grey, one blue, a sidebar, KPI tiles, a table.
materials: KPI tiles over a data table
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar, KPI row, then the inbox as a sortable table with status pills.
canonCard.risk: Looks the same as every competitor by design.
